tasks.title: A multiplier factory
tasks.statement: Write a function make_multiplier(n) that returns a function multiplying its argument by n.
tasks.hint: Define def mul(x): return x * n inside and return mul.

tasks.title: A counter with state
tasks.statement: Write a function make_counter(start=0) that returns a function; each call of it returns the next number, starting from start + 1. The state is kept in the closure (nonlocal); every counter has its own.
tasks.hint: count = start; inside inner: nonlocal count; count += 1; return count.

tasks.title: An accumulator
tasks.statement: Write a function make_accumulator() that returns a function which takes a number, adds it to the accumulated sum (kept in the closure) and returns the current sum.
tasks.hint: total = 0 in the outer function; nonlocal total in the inner one.

tasks.title: A call-counting decorator
tasks.statement: Write a decorator count_calls: after each call of the decorated function, the attribute wrapper.calls grows by one (starting from 0). The function's arguments and result must be preserved.
tasks.hint: Set wrapper.calls = 0 after defining wrapper; inside wrapper: wrapper.calls += 1.

tasks.title: A decorator with a log
tasks.statement: Write a decorator logged: before each call it prints «вызов <имя функции>» (that is, the Russian word «вызов», a space and the function's name), then calls the function and returns its result. The function's name and docstring must be preserved (functools.wraps).

tasks.title: A decorator with a parameter
tasks.statement: Write a decorator repeat(times): it calls the function times times in a row and returns the result of the last call.

tasks.title: Caching
tasks.statement: Write a decorator memoize: it remembers the results of a one-argument function in a dictionary; a repeated call with the same argument does not call the function again.
tasks.hint: cache = {} in the decorator; in wrapper: if n not in cache: cache[n] = func(n); return cache[n].

tasks.title: Positive only
tasks.statement: Write a decorator positive_only: if at least one positional argument is less than zero, it raises ValueError; otherwise it calls the function and returns the result.
tasks.hint: In wrapper: for a in args: if a < 0: raise ValueError(...).
